bc_eastpost_spire.blurb: Eastpost Spire is a tall, slender peak at the south end of Bugaboo Provincial Park in the Purcell Mountains, on the far side of Crescent Glacier from the main Bugaboo group. It has five routes: four trad and one alpine line, with grades from around 5.6 up to a single 5.12 and a pair at 5.10. Trips here run out and back from the Applebee Dome camp in a day. The ridges also give an unroped scramble with one short, exposed fourth-class move near the top, which suits an easy day between bigger objectives.

bc_golden_gate_crag.blurb: Golden Gate Crag is a small trad area above Squamish, in the upper Olesen Creek drainage, off the Mamquam forest road that branches east a little north of the Stawamus Chief. There are five routes, four of them around 5.10 and one at 5.11. Several climb in multiple pitches, linking cracks of different widths, so a standard trad rack and some stamina for sustained crack climbing are the main requirements. It is a place for climbers already comfortable on 5.10 who want longer crack lines away from the busier Squamish walls.

bc_roadside_attraction.blurb: Roadside Attraction is a short bluff in the Fraser Valley, in the Abbotsford and Mission area along Morris Valley Road, with no walk to the base. The wall gets sun from morning into mid-afternoon. This area has five routes: three sport lines around 5.11, one trad route at 5.9 and one aid line. The routes are single-pitch and suit a 60 m rope and a standard set of quickdraws. It works as a quick stop for a few pitches rather than a full day's destination.
